newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda shares slide on cloudy outlook.
newsitem.headline: Honda shares slide on cloudy outlook.

text.p: Shares of Honda Motor Co Ltd fell sharply in heavy trade on Friday morning on expectations that exports by Japanese carmakers could slow down in the future amid growing U.S. concerns about Japan's rising trade surplus, traders said.
Honda had lost 130 yen to 3,110 by 0111 GMT, making it the fifth largest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Volume was 2.478 million shares, making it the fourth-most actively traded issue.

A trader at a foreign securities house said that since Honda announced earlier this week it was considering lowering its production plan for July, some investors had become worried about its future earnings prospects.
Some brokers said the share price was weighed down by worries about the U.S. reaction to Japan's rising trade surplus.
A White House aide told reporters in Denver on Thursday that U.S. President Bill Clinton voiced concern to Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about Japan's surplus.
